mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, no significant negative excess returns in similar tightening events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, boosting consumer confidence and driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 10 similar historical episodes, no 60-day forward return outperforms the 2-month moving average by more than 1.5 percentage points (mean IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (units of new orders) of at least 10% coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak order flow signals impending market softening.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥10% in a month
failure_condition: Across 15 prior demand shocks, no 20-day negative return exceeds 2 standard deviations below the pre-shock mean (IC > -0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in INDPRO above 105 followed by a subsequent month below 100 indicates cyclical supply-side easing, which precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 105 and falls below 100 in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 historical supply easing episodes, no 5-day positive return exceeds 1.5% when the pattern occurs (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by more than 0.25% in the same month, the combined signal of higher inflation expectations and persistent policy accommodation is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↑ > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL ↑ > 0.25% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual inflation and policy accommodation shock
failure_condition: In 50 similar co-movement events, no 20-day return outperforms the average by more than 2% (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (labor market participation) of at least 2% in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as reduced labor supply dampens economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥2% in a month
failure_condition: Over 40 historical participation contractions, no 60-day negative return exceeds -1.2% (IC > -0.08).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP momentum) grows by more than 8% in a quarter followed by two quarters of flat or negative growth, the delayed impact is a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows >8% in Q, then next two quarters ≤0%
failure_condition: In 30 prior late-cycle accelerations, no 20-day return exceeds +1.5% above the pre-acceleration 20-day mean (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in RSAFS (retail sales) below 100 (first month <90, second month <95) in consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent softening in consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 90 in month 1 AND RSAFS < 95 in month 2 (consecutive)
failure_condition: Across 25 historical double-dip RSAFS events, no 60-day negative return exceeds -0.8% (IC > -0.12).
